subject: Intermittent backpressure affecting live chat — update & guidance
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Hoffman <sarah@brightline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent backpressure affecting live chat — update & guidance

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for flagging the issue this morning. We’ve confirmed a pattern of intermittent backpressure on the live-streaming pipeline that can cause delayed or batched chunks to arrive in bursts (appears as perceived lag in your UI). The core impact is higher end-to-end chunk latency during sustained peak token rates, not dropped content.

Immediate actions we’re taking on our side (ETA noted):
- Scoped and isolated problematic edge shard; mitigation target: 30 minutes
- Enabled a temporary throttling smoothing layer on the ingress router (completed)
- Scheduled a short-lived Dedicated burst capacity allotment for Brightline (in progress; 15–30 min to propagate)

Short-term mitigations you can apply immediately (no release required):
1) Reduce client-side chunk buffer window and reassembly timeout. Set stream_chunk_timeout=5000ms to avoid UI stalls.
2) If your UI can tolerate slightly increased latency for critical flows, switch critical endpoints to non-streaming polling for the next 1–2 hours. Polling will avoid chunk reassembly issues while we stabilize the pipeline.
3) For sessions where you must keep streaming, lower max_tokens_per_chunk to 64 for high-throughput sessions. This reduces variability in token cadence.
4) Turn on prefix-based KV caching for repeat prompts (we can toggle this remotely for your account).

We’ve attached a diagnostic bundle (incident-logs-20280527.zip) with request IDs that match your examples — please send any additional request IDs or sample payloads you’ve collected. If you’d like, we can apply the client-side snippet below via a short-hand script or provide a one-line toggle for your engineering team.

Quick example config (client-side):
- stream_chunk_timeout: 5000
- max_tokens_per_chunk: 64
- enable_prefix_cache: true

We’ll keep this thread updated and will share a short postmortem with action items within 72 hours. If impact increases, we’ll escalate to an incident bridge.

Apologies for the disruption — we know real-time UX is critical for Brightline’s agent workflows.

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sarah Hoffman <sarah@brightline.com>

Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 09:34:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent backpressure affecting live chat — update & guidance

Thanks Jasmine — appreciate the rapid response. We saw the first noticeable degradation at ~08:50 PDT on our east-coast peak and it recurred around 08:58 and 09:08. We’ll try the config changes you suggested and report back.

Two quick Qs:
1) Will switching a flow to polling create additional cost for us?
2) Can you confirm whether any customer data was delayed beyond 5 minutes for ingestion to the logs?

I’ve attached one request trace we captured (req-20280527-ax3f). We’ll start toggling the chunk timeout on a small canary.

— Sarah
Sarah Hoffman
Head of Platform, Brightline
sarah@brightline.com

Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 09:47:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent backpressure affecting live chat — update & guidance

Hi Sarah —

Answers: 
1) Polling will increase token consumption slightly for the same conversational exchange because of repeated short-poll requests; we’re happy to credit the incremental cost for the affected window — I’ll confirm with billing and follow up in this thread by EOD.
2) No evidence of >5 minute ingestion delays to persistent logs; logs show chunk reordering and batching at the edge but the store confirmed eventual consistency within 2–3 minutes for all affected requests. We’ll include precise timestamps in the postmortem.

Thanks for the trace — we matched req-20280527-ax3f to an edge shard that had queued bursts. Two next quick options we can toggle for you remotely (confirm which you want):
- Remote toggle A: enable_prefix_cache=true (low risk, immediate)
- Remote toggle B: apply smoothing throttle at the per-account router (medium risk, immediate rollback available)

If you’d like the config patch applied immediately for all sessions, reply ALL: APPLY and we’ll perform the change and monitor. Otherwise we recommend a canary first (apply to 5% traffic).

We’ve also scheduled a 1-hour elevated-support window starting 10:00 PDT to monitor post-change metrics. I’ll post the bridge link in this thread if we need it.

— Jasmine

Attachment: stream-config-patch.txt (small patch containing the client-side snippet)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent backpressure affecting live chat — coordination for postmortem

Marissa — forwarding the thread and customer responses. Brightline accepted the canary approach and we applied enable_prefix_cache remotely to 5% of traffic at 10:05 PDT; initial telemetry shows reduced burstiness on the canary. They will roll to 100% if metrics are green within 20 minutes.

Please action the following for the postmortem: 
- Schedule a 60 minute postmortem with Brightline and infra (suggest 2028-05-28 10:00 PDT)
- Capture the ingress router metrics, edge-shard queuing histograms, and the kernel scheduler logs for 08:30–10:30 PDT
- Add a remediation item: automated smoothing layer (feature request + owner) and a default client snippet to mitigate token cadence variance

I’ve attached the diagnostic bundle we collected. I recommend we include a small customer goodwill credit for the affected 40-minute window (I’ll draft the note if you want).

— Jasmine
